about: What a person, a place or an object is known for: a few clauses, each with the verses that say it, in English, Ukrainian, German and Spanish, written by a language model and read twice more. Nothing here is shown on the site until it is approved: an entry answered 'approved' is loaded by the next load of the known-for step, one answered 'rejected' is not. 'declined' lists the records the first reading gave no line, with its reason.
source: Essenthos, what a record is known for, written from its verses in the King James Version with the verses each clause rests on by claude-sonnet-5-5 on 2026-10-25, read again clause by clause against those verses and rendered into Ukrainian, German and Spanish by a second, separate reading, the renderings read by a third; on the project owner's instruction, each record shown once he has approved it

first.reason: Aaron's life is told at length, so four chief deeds beyond the summary are given: the rod before Pharaoh, the golden calf, the atoning incense, and his death.

second.why: The cited verses 7:11-12 are about the magicians; the rod becoming a serpent is in 7:10 alone.

first.reason: The verses tell of Joshua's long career as Moses' successor, and the chief deeds can be stated from them without repeating the summary.
doubts: Verses naming Jehoshuah in 1 Chronicles 7:27, Jeshua in Nehemiah 8:17 and Jesus in Acts 7:45 and Hebrews 4:8 were left aside; the first is a different Ephraimite in a genealogy, and the others only mention Joshua incidentally.
Number of clauses kept to five for a life told at length; the Gibeon league, the sun standing still and Achan's stoning were left out as lesser.

second.why: Rephidim is named in EXO 17:8, outside the citation, and verses 11-12 are far more than the clause needs.

second.why: Canaan is not named, and 'unbelieving' is not stated; the verses say the spies gave an evil report and died of plague.

declined.name: Hazeroth
declined.reason: The verses mention Hazeroth only as a stage of Israel's journey, and none of them states that the story of Miriam and Aaron happened there.

declined.name: Dor
declined.reason: The verses only name Dor in lists of kings, towns, borders and Solomon's districts, with nothing that happened there beyond the summary.

declined.name: Hushah
declined.reason: The verses only name Hushah as a settlement in a genealogy and as the origin of men called Hushathites, and nothing happened at or to the place itself.

declined.name: Jarmuth
declined.reason: The verses mention Jarmuth only as the seat of one of five allied kings and in lists of kings and towns, so nothing happens to the city itself beyond what the summary says.

declined.name: Jeshimon
declined.reason: The verses use Jeshimon only as a landmark for locating Pisgah, Peor and Hachilah, and nothing is said to happen there or to it.

declined.name: Rahab
declined.reason: These poetic verses use Rahab as a figure for Egypt or a sea monster, or mention it in a list of nations, so they state no event of a place.

declined.name: Kirjath-sannah
declined.reason: the second reading dropped every clause: The cited verses speak of Kirjathsepher (Debir) and never name Kirjath-sannah, so they cannot support the clause for this record.

declined.name: Altar El-elohe-Israel
declined.reason: The only verse says Jacob erected the altar and named it, which the summary already states, so nothing further is told of the altar.
